A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAFE framework. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across additions, moves, and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark accuracies, latency measurements, sharpening and sequence-length ablations, and qualitative outputs. Its appendices include additional latency and 32B-model results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical evaluations and adds sharpening-threshold and geometric-mean results in Table 5. Original latency, larger-model, and qualitative results remain in the appendices.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 adds geometric-mean aggregation as an alternative to prefix-based probability redistribution. New Appendix H specifies weighted-aggregation and speculative-sampling acceptance variants. These extend the existing Generate–Verify–Ensemble procedure; the main experiments retain the original heuristic sharpening.

E1.justification: Both versions use MMLU-redux, MATH500, GSM8K, BBH, ARC-C, and the Oxford 5000 tokenization analysis. The evaluated tokenizer scenarios and appendix task coverage are retained. Appendix H's proposed sampling and weighting extensions are not additional evaluated scenarios.

E2.justification: GaC, UniTE, and the individual-model benchmark comparators remain unchanged. Within the sharpening study, new Table 5 adds an evaluated geometric-mean alternative to the original heuristic and no-sharpening comparisons. Newly cited speculative-decoding and span-level methods are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The added sharpening experiment tests thresholds 0.2 and 0.3 alongside the retained 0.1 setting and geometric-mean aggregation. Cross-benchmark average accuracy is also added. Existing prompts, subject selections, model configurations, greedy decoding, five-token drafting, and the 2048-token limit remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v1 tests sharpening versus no sharpening; v2 extends this analysis with threshold sensitivity and an alternative aggregation strategy in Table 5. The drafting-length ablation, latency analyses, and qualitative cases are retained, including material renumbered or given a separate appendix heading.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added average-accuracy columns summarize benchmarks rather than introduce run-level uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: New Table 5 reports threshold variants and geometric-mean accuracies of 78.31, 77.6, and 92.27 on MMLU-redux, MATH500, and GSM8K. Table 2 adds average-accuracy entries. Matched original per-benchmark scores, latency plots, larger-model results, and qualitative outputs are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation (1) revises the verifier-boundary indexing and quantified range. Appendix H adds formal weighted-probability and stochastic acceptance criteria. Theorem 1 and its proof in Appendix C remain substantively unchanged; no new proof accompanies these extensions.

C1.justification: The introduction removes the specific claim of a 5.72% average CoT improvement while retaining qualitative superiority. The abstract also generalizes the sharpening contribution from introducing prefix consolidation to applying sharpening. The central claims about selective ensembling, stability, and efficiency remain.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 adds explanations for geometric-mean sharpening and why high thresholds reduce sharpening's usefulness, treating strategy choice as flexible. Appendices I–J clarify the scope of OOV-like tokens and the granularity advantage claimed over span-level ensembling. Appendix B's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability statement and repository link in the abstract. It explicitly identifies heuristic sharpening with threshold 0.1 as the main-result configuration. That threshold, the hardware and decoding settings, prompts, and KV-cache description were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning through a dedicated speculative-decoding subsection and new appendices distinguishing SAFE from non-canonical tokenization research and span-level ensembles. These additions discuss several newly cited research directions and articulate specific differences in acceptance criteria, tokenization scope, and ensemble granularity.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites clarify verification, efficiency, and sharpening. Related work gains a new hierarchy, experimental settings move before implementation, and appendix organization gains additional headings and discussions. The overall narrative and most existing exposition remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 5 and an average-accuracy column to Table 2, adjusts captions and running headers, and relocates several existing displays as text flows differently. The ten existing figures retain their graphical content; subsequent tables are renumbered.

improvement.justification: Table 5 provides useful evidence about sharpening choices beyond v1's on/off ablation. Expanded research positioning, clearer explanations, and the code-access statement also improve the paper. These are targeted gains over an otherwise retained empirical foundation. The new discussion slightly overstates consistent sharpening gains: threshold 0.3 averages 81.90 versus 81.93 without sharpening.
